_label_validation.method: 40 poster frames per class drawn at random (seed 11) from own-announcement video posts with features, read by eye on contact sheets by the worker (one reader, no second opinion); the class rule was fixed on a different sample (the 900 oldest frames) before this read

ui.definition: product UI on screen: app, website, editor, terminal, chat (a screen recording or UI mock-up)
ui.misses: a grid of simulation clips, a chat-bubble graphic, a title card, a slide diagram

face.definition: a real person is the subject of the frame

stricter.definition: a person addressing the camera or being interviewed (talking head)

face.misses: a car with a caption, a title card with a portrait thumbnail, an animated character, a room with a distant figure; under the stricter reading also film stills, memes and generated portraits

title.definition: a title card or logo: a product name, headline or mark on a plain or decorative background
title.misses: a quiz graphic, a captioned film still, an aerial shot with a word on it, a textless gold sphere

graphic.definition: motion graphics, a 3D render, an illustration, game footage or generated imagery
graphic.misses: three frames of real people, real footage with a caption, three UI frames

real.definition: real-world footage without a person in close-up: hardware, a robot, a room, a stage, outdoors
real.misses: two title cards, two app graphics, a render

other.definition: nothing much visible: an empty, near-black, blank or barely started frame
other.misses: dim UI screenshots, a pixel-art scene, a line illustration, a dark render

chart.note: 12 announcement videos and about 1% of all frames: too few to validate or analyse

has_face.definition: a human face is visible in the first frame (OpenCV YuNet detector)
has_face.misses: drawn characters, an avatar, a collage

empty_first.definition: a bare first frame: black, blank, or a small mark on a flat background, with no readable text

stricter.definition: nothing visible at all (black or blank)

empty_first.misses: dim UI screenshots in which the text detector found nothing

lower_text_nonui.definition: intended as a proxy for burned-in captions: text in the lower third of a non-UI first frame
lower_text_nonui.verdict: NOT a caption detector: 14 of 40 frames carry a spoken-word caption; the rest are name cards, titles, logos and labels. The attribute is reported only as 'text in the lower third'; burned-in captions are unmeasured.

attributes.from_the_media_record: portrait/square/landscape, 16:9, 1080 px, under 720 px, GIF, upload route are read from the poster's pixel size, the corpus media record and the thumbnail URL; no model involved

big_headline.definition: a headline-size line of readable text in the first frame (a product name, title or headline; a detected text line at least 8% of the frame height tall)
big_headline.misses: small labels, a UI screen, an article page, a table, small-print titles

thumbnails.route: pbs.twimg.com poster-frame URL stored in the corpus row (media[].url)
thumbnails.note: -1 is a network or decode error; 404 a poster that no longer exists

video_files.route_tested: cdn.syndication.twimg.com/tweet-result?id=<post id>&token=<derived from the id> (the public endpoint behind embedded posts; no login, cookie or key)
video_files.test: 6 launch video posts of the corpus, one request each, 1 second apart: 6 of 6 returned HTTP 200 with mediaDetails.video_info: duration_millis, aspect ratio, an HLS playlist and 3 to 5 mp4 variants on video.twimg.com (270p at 256 kbit/s up to 1080p at 10 Mbit/s; one 2160p at 25 Mbit/s). Durations seen: 7.2 s, 14.0 s, 14.6 s, 41.8 s, 70.0 s, 260.5 s.
video_files.bulk: not run. The fetcher for all target posts was refused by this session's permission classifier ('Unauthorized Access') before it started; the refusal was not worked around. No mp4 was downloaded, so there is no duration, bitrate, has_audio, cut, motion or audio feature for any post, and no audio track was published.
video_files.what_it_would_take: permission for this fetch in the worker session; then about 8,000 requests at 2.5 a second (under an hour) for metadata, and the 360p variants for frames and audio

_meta.evidence: poster frames (first frame) only; no video files, no audio
_meta.rule: survives = pairs, ratio and adjusted intervals all exclude no effect among launch-type video posts (every account) or among own-announcement video posts of company and founder accounts, same direction among all video posts of company and founder accounts
